evidence: The original `_number` was `isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)`, which admits NaN/inf that json.loads parses; 10bd28b adds the `±sys.float_info.max` range clause, and the agent's reason for a range over `math.isfinite` (which raises OverflowError on 10**400) holds. Flag is a false positive: 18b24c7 adds `timelines` and TIME-4 start-time checks and never touches `_number`, which predates it unchanged.
guidance_note: When a parser admits values that downstream code compares, enumerate every value json.loads can produce for a number (NaN, ±Infinity, arbitrarily wide ints) and reject the uncomparable ones at the parser in the original PR.

evidence: f179c61 replaces CAP-3's inline `asked.refusal(...)` plus its own 'contradicted its own declaration' text with `_refused_own_endpoint(asked, endpoint)` plus its own CAP-4 clause, so one enforcer remains. evidence: f179c61 adds 'and `TIME-2` through `TIME-6`' to both `Asked.refusal`'s docstring and the Verdicts paragraph in docs/conformance-claims.md; the five new claims do route refusals through the same semantics. Flag is a false positive: the stale lists predate 18b24c7, which changes neither.

evidence: 18b24c7's CAP-3 docstring says both 'a malformed timing array or an `audio_base64` that is not base64' are pinned by tests, but only `test_a_malformed_timing_array_breaks_cap_3` existed; f179c61 adds the base64 test. evidence: `Timed.span` is `ends[-1] - starts[0]` and TIME-6's gap is a difference, so a uniform offset cancels in both; f179c61 adds the `abs(objects[0].starts[0]) > _LENGTH_SPREAD_SECONDS` check plus a +37s tamper test, and the agent checked that live starts[0] is 0.0 so it does not false-positive. guidance_note: For each invariant check built from differences, ask what a constant shift of every value does to it, and add one absolute anchor check (here the first start time against zero).

evidence: The class docstring listed 'a fidelity' among proven invariants while the `fidelity` field is documented as 'unnarrowed'; 4a89e80 removes it from the stamp. evidence: This repeats F2. f179c61's diff shows `probe_cap_3` already calling `_refused_own_endpoint`, so 'already fixed' is accurate even though round 1 reviewed 10bd28b. Flag is a false positive: 10bd28b touched only `_number`, the `Timed` docstring and a test.

narrative: A large prober PR that ran into the five-round review cap, so its final head commit was never reviewed. Most findings were real gaps in the original diff: an untested loop or branch, a doc enumeration not updated, a constant-offset blind spot. The agent fixed them well, often with mutation checks. Fix-caused findings came from two places: the NaN fix's test docstring described counterfactual failure paths wrongly (F9, re-raised as F11), and the agent deliberately deferred the length-mismatch test from F4 (F12, F13). Every round after the first also carried findings that existed before review, so no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags here are mostly false positives, because each round reviewed the whole PR and kept finding gaps from the original diff that were never touched.
Openly deferring part of a finding (the length-mismatch test) still cost a re-raise in the next round; finishing it in the same fix was cheaper.
Running out of rounds left the last commit 46274eb unreviewed, so a PR this large would have been better broken up or swept for test coverage before the first review.

evidence: The PR inserted 5 README lines at :36 and ~156 api.py lines, and 3298fcb shows nearly every Source citation shifting (e.g. HEALTH-1 README:51->56, api.py:793->949). The agent measured 36/40 and 38/38 stale and filed the systemic part as a ticket. The content-based remap kept errors that were already in the base, which shows up as F5, F7 and F8.
guidance_note: When inserting lines into a file another doc cites by line number, re-run the citation check in the original PR, and re-verify every citation against its subject rather than only remapping each from base to head.

evidence: The reviewer's `if "GET" in self.methods: self.methods.add("HEAD")` belongs to Starlette's plain `Route`. FastAPI's `APIRoute` sets methods from the decorator only, and the agent's live enumeration shows `/v1/voices methods={'GET'}`. The suggested assertion would have broken a passing test.

Starlette's `Route` defaults a function endpoint with no `methods=` to GET (+HEAD), so FastAPI's docs routes have populated method sets; the agent's live dump shows `{'HEAD','GET'}` on all four. If the reviewer were right, all 11 fall-through tests would return 500.

`path.encode() not in answer.body` is satisfied for `/v1/voices` by `/v1/voices/settings/default`, and both are in `_NAMED_BACK`. The agent showed the false pass and added `_names_path` with a trailing `(?![\w/-])`, but chose to leave out a leading boundary, which F6 then raised.
guidance_note: When replacing a substring match with a boundary match, write the accept/reject table for both sides of the token (longer path after it, prefix before it) before choosing the pattern.

evidence: 3298fcb moved README:615/637/557 to 620/642/562 by the uniform +5, but those were wrong at the base already. The agent agreed that the content remap 'preserved — invisibly — any citation that was already wrong' and moved them to 705/727/652 in 3ccc3e8.
guidance_note: A citation fix that claims 'every citation correct' must read each cited line back against its subject, not only carry it across the diff alignment.

evidence: `_names_path` (the F4 fix) guarded only the trailing side, so `/api/v1/voices` satisfied `/v1/voices`; the agent says it considered and rejected a leading boundary. 3adb70c adds `(?<![\w/-])` and a parametrized head/tail test, each case shown by mutation to pin its own side. The flag names 3298fcb (docs only), but the cause is the F4 fix.
guidance_note: When fixing a substring match with a boundary, guard both sides in the same fix and parametrize the test over each side.

narrative: This PR adds ROUTE-1/ROUTE-2 refusal bodies and probes. Round 0 found real stale line citations and a substring check that could not fail. The agent correctly pushed back on two wrong claims about FastAPI and Starlette methods, using live route dumps. Every round-1 finding came from an incomplete round-0 fix: the citation remap kept errors already in the base (F5, F7), and the path boundary guarded only one side (F6). Round 2 still found more of the same citation class (F8, F11), plus two original-diff issues. The PR is open and none of the round-2 findings has a reply.
guidance_observations: The citation fix claimed 'every citation correct' on the strength of a base-to-head alignment, which by design keeps errors already in the base; reading each citation back would have prevented two rounds of citation findings.

The agent considered the leading-boundary case for `_names_path` and declined it on a hypothetical false-broken worry, then paid a round for it; writing an accept/reject table for both sides up front settles that trade.
The pushbacks on F2 and F3 were sound because they rested on enumerating the live app's routes, not on argument.
